what: Complete 4x4-tile tavern interior for the town: planked floor, timber walls with a 0.9x2.0 door and two windows, a long bar with three stools, two round tables with benches and mugs, a stone hearth with flame, and two hanging lanterns. Players enter through the south door and read the bar immediately from the isometric camera.

dims.basis: measured from the exported GLB; walls on the 1 u grid at ±2, 1 u corner posts close the runs; exactly one 2.5 u storey

views.why: diorama cutaway from the 45-degree isometric camera; the 60 px gameplay read is the bar and hearth silhouette

style_notes: Low-Poly Diorama: chunky, faceted, flat-shaded, saturated palette accents, readable at ~60 px. Palette-only (docs/ART_DIRECTION.md), no textures, no smooth shading. 1 tile = 1 u; player = 1.55 u; storey = 2.5 u; doors 0.9 x 2.0 u; grid 1 u. Base at z=0, centred on (0,0). Never: smooth normals, external textures, invented hues, hidden geometry nobody sees.
notes: Hero: bmesh-authored parts, selective bevel on floor slab and counter top, weighted normals, flat shading and an explicit UV pack. 1468 triangles (1500 assembled budget). Rebuilt each run from scripts/blender/gen_models_v5.py. Review uses front/three_quarter/eye/iso only: the review harness aims focus close-ups from low exterior angles, which cannot see into a four-walled room; the 45-degree iso and eye views are the primary evidence for the interior props. Camera-facing south and east walls are a 1.1 u cutaway (south keeps a full-height 0.9x2.0 door cell); north and west keep three 2.5 u courses.
